title: Extreme startup building with AI: distribution first, specialized agents, zero-cost co-makers
summary: John Rush explains why he replaced hired departments with AI agents, his three-step agent build process (Zapier, agent builder, hardcode), and why he automated distribution first. He also covers specialized vs general agents, co-maker deals, idea validation, and why great products still beat distribution alone.

principles.text: Be your own perfect customer: build tools for yourself, prove they work on you, and only then launch publicly.
principles.quote: I am kind of my own user. So I built all the tools for myself and I use the agents for myself and I show how it works for me and only when it works I launch to the uh public.

principles.text: Automate distribution first. Building can be slow, but SEO and social need months of compounding effort that can't be rushed later.
principles.quote: the thing that can't wait is distribution because it's not like you will build your tool bring to the market and suddenly it will sell itself right.

principles.text: Build agents in three steps: prototype in Zapier as the broker, move to an agent builder, then hardcode it in regular code.
principles.quote: So then usually I take what I built in Zapier and I connect that into uh this no code AI tool builder thing that I I put them together and users can use it.

principles.text: Specialized agents beat general ones: you know what to expect, so you can hardcode error catching and tight integrations. Niche keeps getting narrower.
principles.quote: the market will reward the agent that does only one thing really, really well.

principles.text: Team up with developers who lack distribution skills on 50/50 revenue share. No salaries, no upfront cost, no investors.
principles.quote: we own it 50/50 and uh there's no salary so we share the revenue or we share the profits right. So basically there's no upfront cost for me.

principles.text: Two ways to win: huge distribution, or a product so good users recommend it. Distribution alone isn't enough; great products still win.
principles.quote: too many people think that distribution alone is enough and is a solution for all problems but I think the great products are still winning.
